newsitem.title: GERMANY: Canal Plus may quit German Vox but not yet.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus may quit German Vox but not yet.

text.p: French media group Canal Plus on Monday did not rule out its withdrawal from loss-making German commercial television channel Vox, but said it had no plans to do so at the moment.
Responding to a magazine report, a Canal Plus spokesman told Reuters that no partner could pull out of Vox before 1999 without the consent of all the station's partners.
"The company is not really thinking of pulling out completely," the spokesman said, adding that speculation over a withdrawal was not new.
The spokesman added that Canal Plus was satisfied with the results achieved at pay television channel Premiere.
German news magazine Focus reported at the weekend that Canal Plus was considering pulling out of both stations.

The Paris-based television group owns 24.9 percent of Vox and 37.5 percent of Premiere -- which is at the centre of a tug of war between Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch and German publishing giant Bertelsmann AG.
Canal Plus confirmed that talks were under way with the Kirch group over a possible reallocation of television interests in Germany and Italy.
Kirch is seeking to dispose of shares in Italy's Telepiu, while Canal Plus could sell shares in Premiere.

A Kirch spokesman declined to comment on this option. But the spokesman did confirm another report that Kirch manager Klaus Piette would take over the chair of the Premiere supervisory board from Gottfried Zmeck.
Zmeck has been seen as facing a conflict of interests on the Premiere supervisory board, since he is also chief executive of Kirch's digital pay television broadcaster DF1.
Kirch owns a minority stake in Premiere -- which is also looking to develop a digital television product -- while it controls DF1 outright.
